The most powerful refutation is **"Pleasures differ in quality, not just quantity."** Bentham's calculus works only if every pleasure and pain can be reduced to one common quantity and summed, and a qualitative difference between pleasures breaks that commensurability. "Pain and pleasure are inevitable features of life" is a descriptive claim that leaves the calculus's method untouched, so it doesn't refute it.

CONFIDENCE: 85
